clue.text: Clear the list of passengers for customs

definitions.text: the list of passengers for customs
definitions.meaning: a document listing a ship's or plane's passengers and cargo for customs officers

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means plain to see; as a noun it is the shipping document declared to customs.

clue.text: Stone found at entrance to a garden?

parts.note: the article a in a garden gives A, the garden being the place the gate leads into
a gate is the entrance to a garden

explanation.surface: A gemstone turns up by a garden gate.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the split: A plus GATE read as 'a garden entrance'.
explanation.definitionFit: This banded chalcedony is a semi-precious stone used in jewellery.

clue.text: Headdress, not wide at the top: wacky but effective

indicators.note: not says a letter is to be left out of the headdress
at the top says the letter dropped is the opening one of the headdress word

parts.note: a wimple is a nun's cloth headdress
W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide
wacky means crazy, mental

explanation.surface: A verdict on a nun's headdress: absurd-looking, yet it does the job.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the opening W from WIMPLE to get IMPLE, then add MENTAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Implemental is an old word for instrumental, serving to bring something about, hence effective.

clue.text: Wind blowing up later? Yes

indicators.note: blowing up suggests the words later and yes are blasted apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the wind will get up later and gets an answer of yes.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Wind' as a verb to the question; it is the definition, a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An easterly is a noun for a wind blowing from the east.

clue.text: In Bethel, they go crazy about start of revivalist hymn

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters go around another piece
crazy tells the letters of In Bethel they go to run wild into a new order
start of picks the opening letter of revivalist

explanation.surface: Worshippers in a chapel called Bethel get carried away over a revivalist hymn.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of INBETHELTHEYGO is placed about R, from 'start of revivalist'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a well-known Easter hymn, set to a tune by Handel.

clue.text: Preparation a help, some say, when applied to receding hair?

indicators.note: when applied to joins the two pieces side by side
receding has the hair word going backwards, as a hairline recedes

parts.note: a mop is a thick mass of hair

indicators.note: some say flags that the letters are what the words sound like

parts.note: a help is an aid

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a hair cream will help a balding man.
explanation.walkthrough: MOP, read backwards, is POM; AID said aloud gives ADE, as in lemonade.
explanation.definitionFit: A preparation is a prepared cosmetic or medicine; this scented hair oil is one.

clue.text: Such language from the terraces getting one down a bit?

indicators.note: down a bit tells the letter for one to slip a place further along in this down light

parts.note: patios are paved terraces beside a house
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Football fans on the terraces swear in a dialect that brings someone down.
explanation.walkthrough: In PATIOS the I moves down one place to give the dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: Patois is a regional dialect, the kind of speech the clue points to.

clue.text: A windy month sometimes causing damage

definitions.meaning: March, famous for wind, is sometimes shortened in dates
to damage or spoil, a verb

explanation.definitionFit: It is the standard abbreviation of the third month and also a verb meaning spoil or impair.

clue.text: Striker, perhaps, put through hell by worker

parts.note: Dis is the classical underworld, hell
taken as written
an ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A footballer is given a hard time by a labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striker' suggests football but means someone on strike, a party to an industrial dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: A disputant is someone engaged in a dispute, as a striking worker is, so a striker is an example.

clue.text: Factions surrounding front of union buildings in Nottingham, say

indicators.note: surrounding says the factions word goes around another piece

parts.note: camps are opposing factions

indicators.note: front of picks the opening letter of union

explanation.surface: Rival groups gather around a student union in Nottingham.
explanation.definitionFit: A university's grounds and buildings, as at Nottingham, form its campus.

clue.text: Excite curiosity among everyone else except husband!

parts.note: among means in

indicators.note: except says the husband letter is left out

parts.note: everyone else is the rest

explanation.surface: Someone stirs up curiosity among all the others, though not the husband.
explanation.definitionFit: To interest someone is to arouse their curiosity, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Keep wild dog

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of keep running loose into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep an untamed dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A peke is a Pekinese, a small toy breed of dog.

clue.text: Trip to the theatre, perhaps, is becoming regular

definitions.meaning: a night out somewhere, a theatre visit being one example
smoothing into an even, level state

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a night out for leisure and also the act of levelling things off.

clue.text: Assorted sugar lumps put in round dish

indicators.note: put in says the round piece goes into the mixed letters
assorted suggests the letters of sugar lumps are mixed up

parts.note: a round shape is O

explanation.surface: A sweet assortment of sugar lumps is put into a bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dish' looks like a bowl but is slang for an attractive person; O goes inside GLAMURPUSS, the rearranged SUGARLUMPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Dish is slang for a good-looking person, as is the glamour word for a glamorous one.

clue.text: A wake-up call for Tommy

parts.note: Tommy is the nickname for a British soldier, so this is the bugle signal that rouses troops in the morning

explanation.definitionFit: The bugle call that wakes soldiers at dawn is the military morning signal.

clue.text: English party has to make speech very detailed

parts.note: Lab is short for Labour, the British political party
to orate is to make a speech

explanation.surface: An English political party has to deliver a speech in great detail.
explanation.walkthrough: LAB is short for Labour, a UK political party.
explanation.definitionFit: Elaborate as an adjective means intricate and worked out in great detail.

annotationWithheld.clue: With cross, honours a war hero

clue.text: Pole at boxing venue, practising for the fight

parts.note: a spar is a pole, as on a ship
boxers fight in a ring

explanation.surface: A post at a boxing hall is used for training before a bout.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparring is boxing practice with a partner before a real contest.

clue.text: Like taking part in gym lesson and history

indicators.note: taking part in places the like word within the gym lesson

parts.note: PT is physical training, the school gym lesson
like means as

explanation.surface: Comparing joining in a gym class with studying history.
explanation.definitionFit: The past is everything that has happened before now, the subject of history.

clue.text: She produced sculptures with it, at a price

parts.note: hep is old slang for fashionable or with it
worth means valued at a given price

explanation.surface: A sculptor working fashionably and expensively.
explanation.walkthrough: Barbara Hepworth was a celebrated twentieth-century English sculptor.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbara Hepworth was a leading English modernist sculptor, so she fits the description.

clue.text: Female was company director and leader, once

parts.note: ran means managed, as a director does, and CO is short for company
ran means managed, as a director does, and CO is short for company

explanation.surface: A woman who ran a firm and led it in her day.
explanation.walkthrough: Francisco Franco was Spain's dictator from 1939 to 1975.
explanation.definitionFit: General Franco was Spain's head of state for decades, a former leader.

clue.text: Trip at the public's expense I've understood is standard

parts.note: a jolly is a junket, a trip enjoyed on public money
roger is radio talk for message received and understood

explanation.surface: An official complains that taxpayer-funded jaunts have become the norm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' looks like 'the norm' but is a flag; the pirate flag is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a flag, and this is the skull-and-crossbones flag flown by pirates.

clue.text: Unattractive woman's first to hide bottom

indicators.note: first to hide says the opening letter of the woman word disappears

parts.note: a frump is a dowdy, unattractive woman

explanation.surface: A plain woman is the first to cover her behind.
explanation.definitionFit: The rump is the hindquarters, a synonym for the bottom.

clue.text: Short magazine article about new cartoon genre

indicators.note: about says the magazine and article letters go round the new piece

parts.note: mag is short for magazine
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A brief magazine piece reports on a fresh style of cartoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Manga is the Japanese style of comic book and cartoon art.

clue.text: Even in cooler, getting turn to dance

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the cooler word

parts.note: a fan cools the air
and can carry the sense of even, as in archaic usage meaning also
a go is a turn

explanation.surface: Getting a turn on the dance floor even in the cool room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Even' is the odd piece: AND in the old sense of also or even, put inside FAN before GO is added.
explanation.definitionFit: The fandango is a lively Spanish courtship dance in triple time.

clue.text: Note something for carrying bricks up

indicators.note: up, in a down light, says the bricks carrier is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a hod is a builder's trough for carrying bricks

explanation.surface: A note about a gadget for lifting bricks.
explanation.definitionFit: Doh is the first note of the tonic sol-fa scale.

clue.text: Creature found in Antigua, naturally

indicators.note: found in says the creature lies within the next words

explanation.surface: A creature that lives in Antigua as a matter of course.
explanation.definitionFit: The iguana is a large tropical lizard, a creature of the Caribbean.

clue.text: After college, turned on loud music

indicators.note: after places the reversed piece behind the college

parts.note: a tech is a technical college

indicators.note: turned says the word on is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone, having left college, discovers a taste for loud music.
explanation.definitionFit: Techno is a loud electronic dance music style.

clue.text: Setback for man, old low-paid worker finally expelled from Croatia?

indicators.note: setback says the man word goes backwards

parts.note: a guy is a man

indicators.note: finally expelled says the last letter of the worker word is removed

parts.note: a slave is a worker paid little or nothing

explanation.surface: A man in old Croatia suffers a setback as a poorly paid labourer is thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: GUY backwards is YUG; SLAVE without its last letter is SLAV. The question mark admits Croatia was only part of the old federation.
explanation.definitionFit: Croatia was once part of the Yugoslav federation, so something from there could be described this way.
